questions.stem: A manufacturer's feasible region has corner points $(0,0)$, $(7,0)$, $(4,3)$ and $(0,5)$. Find the largest value of the profit function $Z = 2x + 5y$ over this region.
questions.explanation: For a bounded feasible region the optimum of a linear objective is reached at a corner point, so evaluate $Z$ at each one: $0$, $14$, $23$ and $25$ respectively. The largest of these is $25$, attained at $(0,5)$.

optionRationale.1: This is $Z$ at $(4,3)$ only; the corner $(0,5)$ gives a larger value.
optionRationale.2: This is $Z$ at $(7,0)$ and is not the largest of the four corner values.
optionRationale.3: No corner gives $29$; this comes from adding $2\cdot 7$ and $5\cdot 3$, which are coordinates of different corners.

questions.objective: Evaluate a linear objective at the corner points of a bounded region

questions.stem: The origin satisfies the constraint $3x + 4y \le 12$, so the half-plane of this constraint lies on the same side of the line as the origin. Which of the following points belongs to this half-plane?
questions.explanation: Substitute each point into $3x + 4y$ and compare with $12$. For $(1,2)$ the value is $11 \le 12$, so it lies in the half-plane. The other three points give $14$, $16$ and $17$, all larger than $12$, so they lie on the far side of the line.

optionRationale.2: $3(2)+4(2)=14$, which is more than $12$, so this point is outside.
optionRationale.3: $3(4)+4(1)=16$, which exceeds $12$, so it is outside.
optionRationale.4: $3(3)+4(2)=17$, which exceeds $12$, so it is outside.

questions.objective: Identify the half-plane of a linear inequality using a test point

questions.stem: A workshop is restricted by $x + y \le 7$ and $2x + y \le 12$ with $x, y \ge 0$. What is the maximum of $Z = 3x + 4y$ under these restrictions?
questions.explanation: The corner points are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(5,2)$ and $(0,7)$, where $Z$ equals $0$, $18$, $23$ and $28$. The maximum is $28$ at $(0,7)$. Because $y$ has the larger coefficient, the optimum favours the corner with the most $y$.

optionRationale.2: $23$ is the value at $(5,2)$, the point where the two lines cross, but $(0,7)$ gives more.
optionRationale.3: $18$ is the value at $(6,0)$ only, the corner with the most $x$.
optionRationale.4: $46$ would need $x=6$ and $y=7$ together, which breaks both constraints.

questions.objective: Solve a two-constraint maximisation by the corner point method

questions.stem: Over the unbounded region $x + y \ge 6$, $x + 3y \ge 10$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$, the cost function is $Z = 5x + 2y$. Its minimum value is
questions.explanation: The corner points are $(0,6)$, $(4,2)$ and $(10,0)$, giving $Z = 12$, $24$ and $50$. Since both coefficients are positive, $Z$ cannot fall towards $-\infty$ in the unbounded direction, so the least corner value $12$ at $(0,6)$ is the minimum.

optionRationale.1: $24$ is the value at the crossing point $(4,2)$; the corner $(0,6)$ is cheaper.
optionRationale.2: $50$ is the value at $(10,0)$, the largest of the three corner values.
optionRationale.3: $30$ is $5\cdot 6$, obtained by wrongly putting the $y$-intercept into the $x$ term.

questions.objective: Find the minimum of a cost function over an unbounded region

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): If the objective $Z = ax + by$ takes the same maximum value at two adjacent corner points, it takes that maximum value at every point of the segment joining them.
Reason (R): The value of a linear function at a point of a line segment is a weighted average of its values at the two end points.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: A point $P$ on the segment equals $tA + (1-t)B$ with $0 \le t \le 1$, and linearity gives $Z(P) = tZ(A) + (1-t)Z(B)$. When $Z(A) = Z(B) = M$ this equals $M$ for every $t$, so the assertion holds and the weighted-average property of the reason is exactly why.

optionRationale.2: The reason is not just true; it is the argument that proves the assertion.
optionRationale.3: The reason is true, since linearity gives a weighted average along a segment.
optionRationale.4: The assertion is true: such an LPP has infinitely many optimal points.

questions.objective: Explain multiple optimal solutions of an LPP

questions.stem: Each pair of boundary lines in List-I meets at a corner point of some feasible region. Match the pair with its corner point in List-II.
questions.explanation: Solve each pair of equations. A: adding gives $2x = 8$, so $(4,2)$. B: $x = 2$ gives $y = 4$, so $(2,4)$. C: $y = 3$ gives $x = 4$, so $(4,3)$. D: subtracting gives $2x = 4$, so $x = 2$ and $y = 6$. Hence A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

optionRationale.1: Items A and B have been interchanged; check each pairing against its definition.
optionRationale.3: Items C and D have been interchanged; check each pairing against its definition.
optionRationale.4: Items A and C have been interchanged; check each pairing against its definition.

questions.objective: Locate corner points as intersections of boundary lines

questions.stem:
A bounded feasible region has corner points $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(4,4)$ and $(0,5)$ and the objective is $Z = 3x + 2y$. Consider:
A. The maximum of $Z$ is $20$, attained at $(4,4)$.
B. The minimum of $Z$ is $0$, attained at the origin.
C. $Z$ is greater at $(0,5)$ than at $(6,0)$.
D. $Z$ attains its maximum at two different corner points.
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: The corner values of $Z$ are $0$, $18$, $20$ and $10$. The maximum $20$ is unique at $(4,4)$ and the minimum $0$ is at the origin, so A and B are true. At $(0,5)$ $Z = 10$ is less than $18$ at $(6,0)$, so C is false, and no tie exists, so D is false.

optionRationale.1: C is false because $Z(0,5) = 10$ is less than $Z(6,0) = 18$.
optionRationale.3: D is false because the maximum value $20$ occurs at one corner only.
optionRationale.4: C is false, so the three statements cannot all hold.

questions.objective: Compare corner values of an objective function

questions.stem: The corner points of a feasible region are $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(3,4)$ and $(0,5)$. The function $Z = px + qy$ with $p, q > 0$ gives the same maximum value at $(6,0)$ and $(3,4)$. The ratio $p : q$ is
questions.explanation: Equal values at the two corners give $6p = 3p + 4q$, so $3p = 4q$ and $p : q = 4 : 3$. Check the other corner: with $p = 4$, $q = 3$ the value at $(0,5)$ is $15$, below the common maximum $24$, so these two corners really are optimal.

optionRationale.1: This inverts the ratio; $3p = 4q$ means $p$ is the larger one.
optionRationale.2: With $p = 2q$ the values are $6p = 12q$ and $3p + 4q = 10q$, which are unequal.
optionRationale.3: With $p : q = 6 : 5$ the values are $36$ and $38$ for $p=6$, $q=5$, so the tie condition fails.

questions.objective: Find the objective coefficients that give two optimal corners

questions.stem: The feasible region of an LPP is given by $x + 2y \le 10$, $3x + y \le 15$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$. Its area in square units is
questions.explanation: The vertices are $(0,0)$, $(5,0)$, $(4,3)$ and $(0,5)$. The two slanted lines meet at $(4,3)$. By the shoelace formula the area is $\tfrac12|(0\cdot0-5\cdot0)+(5\cdot3-4\cdot0)+(4\cdot5-0\cdot3)+0| = \tfrac12(15+20) = 17.5$.

optionRationale.1: $25$ is the area of a $5 \times 5$ square, which the region does not fill.
optionRationale.2: $15$ is only the area of triangle $(0,0),(5,0),(4,3)$, which leaves out the upper triangle.
optionRationale.4: $20$ does not follow from the shoelace sum, which is $35$ before halving.

questions.objective: Compute the area of a feasible region from its vertices

questions.stem: Maximise $Z = 4x + 3y$ subject to $x + y \le 10$, $2x + y \le 14$, $x \le 6$, $x \ge 0$, $y \ge 0$. The maximum value is
questions.explanation: The region has five corner points: $(0,0)$, $(6,0)$, $(6,2)$, $(4,6)$ and $(0,10)$. Their $Z$ values are $0$, $24$, $30$, $34$ and $30$. The largest is $34$ at $(4,6)$, where $x+y=10$ and $2x+y=14$ meet.

optionRationale.1: $30$ occurs at both $(6,2)$ and $(0,10)$, but $(4,6)$ gives more.
optionRationale.3: $24$ is the value at $(6,0)$, a corner with $y = 0$.
optionRationale.4: $38$ is above every corner value, so it is not attained in the region.
